analysis.title: "Please Don't Stop The Museic": Everything You Need To Know Ahead Of Meta's Earnings
key_insights: Meta reports Q3 earnings on the evening of Oct 21, 2026, a week earlier than usual. JPMorgan's Schilsky grades investor expectations 9 out of 10, the highest of the big Internet names reporting over the next two weeks. Netflix got a 3, Alphabet a 5, and Amazon, Spotify and Etsy a 7 each.

The stock bottomed at $543.67 on Aug 18, rallied about 43% to a $777.59 high on Sep 24 after the Muse launch, and now trades near $708, about 9% below the peak and roughly 30% above the low. It has closed lower in nine of the last 11 sessions and just snapped a five-session losing streak.

Positioning is crowded. Goldman's cash desk has Meta positioning at 8/10, and Mag 7 net exposure on the Goldman Prime book is at a record, about 22% of total US net exposure, even as hedge funds sold Info Tech at the fastest pace in a decade.

Options pricing is modest relative to history. Goldman's derivatives desk puts the implied move at 6.57% against an average realized move of 9.9% over the past 5 prints. Meta has moved at least 8% the day after each of its last five reports, in both directions, and the last two moved down.

The Q3 revenue bar is the high end of Meta's $61-64B guide. Schilsky puts the buyside bogey at about $64B (+26% y/y FX-neutral) and the Street at about $63.25B. Deutsche Bank is at $63.7B and cites ad checks showing CPM growth accelerated about 350bps sequentially in 3Q.

The Q4 revenue guide is expected at $72-75B (Schilsky), with Deutsche hearing a slightly lower top end of roughly $74-74.5B. Street Q4 revenue is about $73.5B (+24% FX-neutral). Investors will tolerate no more than a 1-point FX-neutral deceleration on the top end of the range.

The main debate is 2027 spending, not Q3. Buyside expectations for 2027 opex are $210-230B (guide expected near $215-225B) against Street about $203B. 2027 capex expectations are $225-250B against Street about $200B. Buyside opex plus capex for 2027 is $435-475B (midpoint $455B) against a Street sum of $403B, a gap of more than $50B.

Meta said last year it would stop giving next-year opex and capex guides on the Q3 call, so the 2027 numbers may not appear. Schilsky expects CFO Susan Li to repeat that 2027 capex dollar growth will be 'notably larger' and opex language to shift to growth at a slower rate in 2027 than 2026. He says opex matters more than capex because investors care more about EPS than FCF.

2026 guidance: Schilsky expects the opex guide to be raised by about $10B at both ends because of the attorneys general settlement. Capex is expected near the high end of $130-145B, with the low end possibly lifted to $135B.

Muse monetization is mostly a promise. Schilsky says it may not be meaningful in 2027 and is set to ramp in 2028. Investors want hard Muse KPIs such as DAUs or downloads on the call. Sensor Tower shows 10.9M downloads since launch (10.2M in the US), but daily net user additions have slowed more than 60% from the September surge, and almost 39% of Meta's marketing spend this month went to promoting Muse.

Amazon blocked Meta's agents from its store within two weeks of the Muse launch, and other banks are reportedly following. Bloomberg's Dave Lee says much of Muse's success came from brute-force marketing.

A majority of buyside investors still expect an equity raise after Q3 if the stock is high enough, with above $850 'better' and $800 the rough threshold. $800 is about 13% above the current price and $850 about 20%. UBS asked whether the early report date is an attempt to get ahead of the cap raise crowd.

Debt funding is getting more expensive. The $27B Hyperion data center bond (RPLDCI 6.581% of 2049) hit a lifetime low of 91.5 on Monday, down from 110 a year ago. Goldman Prime shows long-dated Meta paper among the most-shorted US IG bonds, and Goldman's FICC desk says the entire credit market is focused on Meta earnings.

Needham's Laura Martin calculates Meta has $628B of off-balance-sheet commitments against $112B of on-balance-sheet debt and leases. Adding them to enterprise value makes the stock 35% more expensive.

A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25B in the Cambridge Analytica data privacy case hours before the print. The state asked for $35-40B and Meta argued for a cap of $3.45B. This is on top of the roughly $10B attorneys general settlement already headed for the 2026 opex guide. Meta is expected to appeal.

Goldman's Eric Sheridan sees a resilient digital advertising environment into Q3 with solid momentum exiting the quarter, and AI increasingly driving ad share gains. He reiterated Buy and raised his price target to $860 from $725. Deutsche's Benjamin Black (Buy, $820 target) uses 27x 2027E earnings to reflect Muse agent adoption and raised his 2027 capex forecast to $232B from $214B.

Valuation: Bloomberg shows Meta at 19x forward earnings, the second-cheapest Mag 7 stock after Nvidia. The article argues the market is pricing 2028 earnings from a product that will not make meaningful money until 2028, funded by spending that hits 2027 earnings.

Recent reaction history is negative. The last two prints moved the stock -9% and -8%, and the last two Q3 prints moved it -4% and -11%. In July a revenue guide and another capex hike sent the stock down 8%. The article's closing view is that the market keeps paying Meta for products and charging it for the bill.

market_movers.rationale: Goldman's Eric Sheridan reiterated Buy and raised the target to $860 from $725 in his US Digital Ad Q3'26 Preview. He sees a resilient ad environment and AI driving ad share gains.
Deutsche Bank's Benjamin Black values the stock at 27x 2027E earnings to reflect Muse agent adoption. His Q3 revenue estimate is $63.7B and he raised his 2027 capex forecast to $232B from $214B.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman's Sheridan sees a resilient digital ad environment into Q3 with solid momentum exiting the quarter. Deutsche's agency checks show CPM growth accelerating.

earnings_insights: META Q3 2026 (reports Oct 21 after the close). Company revenue guide $61-64B. Street consensus revenue about $63.25B per JPMorgan, Bloomberg median $63.33B, highest sell-side estimate $64.07B. These are estimates, not reported figures.
META Q3 buyside bogey is about $64B revenue (+26% y/y FX-neutral) with a slight upward bias, per JPMorgan's Schilsky. Deutsche Bank estimate is $63.7B.
META Q3 EPS Bloomberg consensus range is $2.61 to $4.43 (estimates). The range is wide, probably because analysts differ on legal charges.
META Q3 capex is expected at $41B (Bloomberg consensus) against less than $19B a year ago.

META Q4 2026 revenue: Street estimate about $73.5B (+24% FX-neutral). JPMorgan expects a guide of $72-75B and Deutsche expects roughly $74-74.5B. These are expectations for guidance, not company figures.

META FY2026 capex guide is currently $130-145B (company guide as of Jul 29, previously $125-145B). Schilsky expects it to end near the high end, with the low end possibly lifted to $135B. Bloomberg consensus is about $140B.
META FY2026 opex guide is expected to be raised by about $10B at both ends because of the attorneys general settlement (JPMorgan expectation).

META 2027 estimates: Street opex about $203B, buyside range $210-230B (JPMorgan), Deutsche says investors expect $210-225B opex. Street capex about $200B (Bloomberg $202B), buyside $225-250B (JPMorgan), Deutsche says $230-240B. Bloomberg 2028 capex is $218B. Street 2027 opex plus capex is $403B against a buyside $435-475B.

META 2027 EPS: Street EPS is about $32 and there are real concerns the first 2027 opex guide knocks it down to about $34 or lower per the Schilsky excerpt, though the source text is garbled on this figure. 2028 EPS estimates are 'in the low 40s' vs the Street's roughly $39 to $40 (figures partly garbled in the source).
META historical earnings-day moves: at least 8% in each of the last five reports. The last two prints were -9% and -8%, and the last two Q3 prints were -4% and -11% (last October).

trade_ideas.rationale: Goldman sees attractive risk-reward because the QQQ straddle prices a 2% move and the META implied move of 6.57% is below the 9.9% average realized move.

risk_factors: A first 2027 opex guide that knocks Street 2027 EPS lower, since opex growth matters more than capex growth to the stock.
Capex language such as 'notably larger' for 2027, and a buyside spending bar about $50B above the Street.
An equity raise after the print, which a majority of the buyside expects if the stock is high enough.
Rising cost of debt, shown by the Hyperion bond at a lifetime low, heavy shorting of long-dated Meta paper, and $628B of off-balance-sheet commitments.
Legal costs, including the $25B New Mexico Cambridge Analytica order and the roughly $10B attorneys general settlement.
Muse growth that may already have peaked, with daily net user additions down more than 60% and heavy marketing spend behind it. Monetization may not be meaningful until 2028.
Crowded positioning (8/10) and a record Mag 7 exposure leave little room for a modest beat.
Free cash flow is projected to be negative until at least 2028 (Bloomberg consensus).
vol_and_positioning: Goldman's derivatives desk (GS Vol Views): META implied earnings move is 6.57%, which 'looks cheap' versus the 9.9% average realized move over the past 5 prints.
Goldman: flat near-term put-call skew at the 20th percentile versus the 10-year history shows constructive positioning.
Friday's QQQ straddle is pricing a 2% move around the Meta print. Goldman's TMT specialists see attractive risk-reward in owning QQQ or META gamma.
Goldman's cash desk has META positioning at 8/10, and the stock remains an overweight for most investors after the post-Muse rally.
Goldman Prime: Mag 7 net exposure hit a record, about 22% of total US net exposure. Info Tech saw the largest 2-week net selling on record for the bank's data, -3.3 standard deviations.

Goldman Prime shows 9 of the 10 most-shorted US IG bonds are long-dated META, NVDA, ORCL, GOOGL and SPCX paper. CoreWeave's 9.25% 2030s are the most-shorted HY bond, and Oracle has the largest IG market value on loan.
The Hyperion data center bond hit a lifetime low of 91.5 on Monday, down from 110 a year ago.
cross_bank_references: Goldman's derivatives desk calls the implied move cheap while JPMorgan's trader grades expectations 9 out of 10, both pointing to a high bar
Deutsche's expectation of 2027 opex $210-225bn and capex $230-240bn is in line with JPMorgan's buyside checks
UBS asked whether Meta reporting a week early is trying to get ahead of the cap raise crowd

tension_points.bull_case: Meta beats toward the $64B high end, guides Q4 to about $75B, gives a Muse DAU number and keeps 2027 vague. The stock grinds to $800 and into equity-raise territory. Goldman sees a resilient ad market and Deutsche's checks show CPM growth accelerating.
tension_points.bear_case: Even with a beat, a 'notably larger' 2027 capex message or a first 2027 opex guide that cuts Street EPS knocks the stock. The last two prints were -9% and -8%, positioning is 8/10 and a majority of the buyside expects an equity raise.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A first 2027 opex guide above the roughly $215-225B buyside range, or capex language of 'notably larger' for 2027 despite a revenue beat.

tension_points.bull_case: Muse has 10.9M downloads, far ahead of ChatGPT, Sora and Gemini at the same post-launch stage on downloads, users and time spent (Deutsche), and a $100 a month Maximum tier is a start on monetization.
tension_points.bear_case: Daily net user additions have slowed more than 60%, Amazon blocked Meta's agents, about 39% of marketing spend goes to promoting Muse, and Schilsky says monetization may not matter until 2028.
tension_points.what_invalidates: No hard Muse KPIs such as DAUs or downloads on the call, which would leave investors without forward user metrics to underwrite the spending.

tension_points.bull_case: A strong print gets the stock into raise territory (above $800, with $850 better) before Microsoft, Amazon and Alphabet report next week.
tension_points.bear_case: The Hyperion bond is at a lifetime low of 91.5, long-dated Meta bonds are heavily shorted, and a raise would be the bill for the AI buildout arriving for shareholders.

theme_stances.key_argument: Expectations are 9 out of 10 and positioning 8 out of 10, so a beat is only the price of admission while the market keeps charging Meta for its spending.
theme_stances.evidence: Can management keep the party going?

theme_stances.key_argument: Buyside expects 2027 opex plus capex of $435-475B against a Street sum of $403B, and opex growth matters more to EPS-focused investors.
theme_stances.evidence: Opex growth matters WAY MORE than Capex growth

theme_stances.key_argument: A majority of investors believe an equity raise is likely post-Q3 if the stock is high enough, since Meta will burn free cash flow next year.
theme_stances.evidence: a majority of investors still believe that an Equity Raise is likely post-Q3
